title: Pandas Series and Labeled Data
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and core concepts of Pandas Series and Labeled Data.
Use the relevant NumPy or pandas APIs to solve a data task.
Inspect shapes, labels, dtypes and missing-value behaviour.
Choose appropriate operations and validate their outputs.
Identify performance, correctness and data-quality limitations.

understand.concept: A pandas Series is a one-dimensional labeled array. It contains values and an index, which can be a default integer index or meaningful labels. Labels make alignment and selection expressive, but labels should be unique when the application expects one-to-one row identity. A Series can contain missing values and may use inferred or explicit dtypes.
understand.whyItMatters: Data analysis depends on choosing correct representations and operations. Understanding these structures helps learners process datasets accurately and explain their results.
understand.analogy: A Series resembles a list with named positions. The labels make values easier to identify, but unlike a simple list, arithmetic and alignment can use index labels rather than only physical positions.
understand.summary: Pandas Series and Labeled Data adds practical library skills to the Python data-analysis workflow.

explain.narrative: Create a Series from a list, dictionary or scalar with an index. Use .loc for label-based selection and .iloc for positional selection. Inspect index, dtype, shape and isna(). Be explicit when a label could be confused with an integer position. Arithmetic between Series aligns labels and may introduce missing values where labels do not match.

examples.title: Create a Series
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
scores = pd.Series([78, 85, 92])
print(scores.tolist())
examples.explanation: A Series stores one-dimensional values with an index.

examples.title: Create labeled values
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
sales = pd.Series([120, 150], index=['East', 'West'])
print(sales.loc['West'])
examples.explanation: loc selects by the index label.

examples.title: Select by position
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
scores = pd.Series([78, 85, 92], index=['A', 'B', 'C'])
print(scores.iloc[1])
examples.explanation: iloc selects the second element by its zero-based position.

examples.title: Filter a Series
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
scores = pd.Series([45, 72, 88])
print(scores[scores >= 60].tolist())
examples.explanation: A boolean condition selects values meeting the threshold.

examples.title: Count missing values
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
values = pd.Series([10, None, 30])
print(int(values.isna().sum()))
examples.explanation: isna() creates a boolean mask and sum() counts missing entries.

practise.guidedTask: Create a Series of five product prices indexed by product code. Retrieve one item by label and one by position, then filter prices above a threshold.
practise.independentTask: Create two Series with partially overlapping region labels. Add them and inspect how pandas aligns the indexes and represents unmatched labels.
hints: Use .loc for labels and .iloc for positions.
Inspect the index before relying on label selection.
Use isna() to detect missing values.
Do not assume integer labels always mean integer positions.
Use explicit dtype when the data contract requires it.
practise.challenge: Build a Series validation helper that checks required labels, missing values and numeric dtype before returning a filtered result.

questions.prompt: What are the two main parts of a Series?
questions.explanation: A Series is one-dimensional and label-indexed.

questions.prompt: How can missing Series values be detected?
questions.explanation: isna() returns a boolean result identifying missing entries.

questions.prompt: What may happen when two Series with different indexes are added?
questions.answer: Values align by labels and unmatched labels can become missing
options: Values align by labels and unmatched labels can become missing
questions.explanation: Pandas arithmetic aligns labeled data by index.
